assertions: The owner shall recover the dog; the dog is not lost for good
The dog is still alive and still in London within the city, not fled far away into the country, because its significator is in a sign of the same triplicity as the Ascendant signifying London
Search to the west, in the southern quarter verging west — the west to south-west part of the city from the owner's home at Temple Bar

The dog is wandering at liberty in an open place rather than stolen away or dead, though for the present hidden from sight, Moon in an airy sign and under the Sun's beams, with Sun and Moon in the 8th raising a false fear of loss
News of or recovery of the dog comes on the following Monday, when the Sun applies by dexter aspect to Saturn, lord of the Ascendant
method: Lilly horary astrology for lost small animals, 6th-house significator, whole-sign/classical horary rules
reasoning: 6th house and its lord signify the small dog. Its significator in a western sign and in the southern quarter verging west gives west verging south as the search direction. Being in a sign of the same triplicity as the Ascendant (London) keeps it still in the city and near at hand, and its application to a trine of the 6th cusp is a friendly application promising return to hand. Moon in an airy sign shows a living animal wandering in the open, under the beams only obscured for now, so the 8th-house Sun and Moon do not overthrow recovery. The Sun applying on the following Monday by dexter aspect to Saturn, lord of the Ascendant, times the querent's getting news/recovery to that Monday.
summary: He shall recover his dog by searching west verging south within London, with recovery or sure news on the following Monday.
